title: Reference amplitude cost model (no native speedup claim)
statement: Under BCM-1, the closed coefficient formula evaluates one reference amplitude in O(R) big-integer operations, the frozen enumeration producer performs exactly sum_{j<R} C(Q-1,j)2^j indicator tests per amplitude call, and all amplitude classes fit in a table of at most QR entries; row assembly is conditional on explicit ring-unit hypotheses.
verified: closed coefficient route equals the frozen enumeration producer on 163,912 bounded calls
row assembly equals the reference route on 10,476 rows over the rationals and Z/25
the required unit hypotheses refuse node 5 modulo 25 and denominator 2 modulo 8
the corrected evidence replays from a clean extraction of the sealed r7 source package and from this repository checkout

Neutral result N1: the closed row-assembly identity is exact on 10,476 orbit rows with zero mismatches but arithmetically neutral, 120,876 ring operations against the reference route's 123,588; the hypothesised quadratic-against-cubic gain was wrong and both routes are quadratic in |E|.

Negative result N3: exact live-column counts place the row-centric crossover above 5.8e5 owners at the centred mismatch count for (A,R,Q)=(17,5,80) and above 5.2e7 for (15,8,80), so the owner-centric route is correct by orders of magnitude at realistic sizes.

B5-M7 is derived from the producer's definition in the repository (revision 0.4.0-candidate): an indicator collapse (689,730 binary and 23,766 ternary cases), the inner-sum collapse (380,464 amplitudes), the parity coefficients in closed form (49 systems) and a binomial identity by the substitution x = z/(1+z) (3,132 cases), each checked by code written from the definitions, with two mutated statements failing as required.
unresolved: external mathematical review; a standalone, separately written step-by-step checker of the B5-M7 derivation now exists (revision 0.4.0-candidate), but it is not externally authored
the later source correspondence and candidate evaluator are a separate discovery line, not a result of this reference-only checker
the historical cost argument's parameter regimes are corrected in revision 0.3.0; at fixed R the enumeration count is polynomial in Q
nonclaims: not a total owner-sum cost theorem
not a claim about an executable native entry
smallest_decisive_test: Reproduce the declared reference checks and audit each asymptotic comparison with its parameter regime; review the separately tracked native evaluator independently.
